newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran's moves threaten Gulf security-GCC official.
newsitem.headline: Iran's moves threaten Gulf security-GCC official.

text.p: Iran's moves to bolster its "occupation" of Gulf islands claimed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) could threaten the oil-rich region's security, a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) official said on Sunday.
The Kuwait News Agency said in a dispatch from Riyadh based on remarks by GCC Secretary-General Jameel al-Hujailan:

"He (Hujailan) warned that continued implementation by the Iran's government of measures to consolidate its occupation of the three UAE islands...would increase military tension in the region and could jeopardise security and stability."

Hujailan has urged Iran to respond to peace initiatives to resolve its dispute with the UAE, which had urged Tehran to take the row over the islands of Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa to the International Court of Justice.

Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable but has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to remove any "misunderstandings". In 1992 the two sides held talks but failed to resolve the dispute.
The GCC, which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and the UAE, supports Abu Dhabi's position in the row.
"Hujailan accused Iran that its practices in reality very often differ from the statements of its officials in which they express desire to build friendly ties with the Council states."
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Friday said non-Arab Iran and former Kuwait occupier Iraq sought control on world oil supplies.

Although some diplomats say Washington had at times overstated any threat from Iran, several Western powers and Gulf Arab states have in the past few months expressed concern over Tehran's growing military might.
Iran is strategically placed at the only entrance to the Gulf, the narrow Strait of Hormuz through which 15 million barrels of oil pass daily.
Moving to Iraq, Hujailan said member countries will not change their position towards Baghdad until it complies with United Nations resolutions related to the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
"Of the most important matters for the leaders of the Council states are the regional issues related to the security and stability of the region," said the agency reporting Hujailan's remarks.
The GCC is to hold its annual summit in the Qatari capital Doha on December 7.
